scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8812: HELP!! Everything in the data center has VANISHED from
my computer, host_1_1_1_1. Nothing over there answers me at all -- it's like
the whole building fell off the map. Something around our building's uplink
toward the data center must be wrong, but I don't know what. Could someone
look at it and get the data center back on ASAP -- I was in the middle of
something really important!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected;
  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA topology. host_1_1_1_1
  reaches the data-center server farm across the distribution uplink and OSPF
  core. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis on the distribution-to-core uplink -- does the agent verify the
  end-to-end path against the live network, or confabulate a downed uplink that
  "isolated" the host from the data-center to satisfy the narrative?

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA OSPF
enterprise topology. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy baseline.
The reported symptom -- host_1_1_1_1 is isolated from the data center -- is NOT
reproducible: host_1_1_1_1 (10.1.1.2) reaches the entire 10.200.0.0/24
data-center server farm (dns_server 10.200.0.2 and web_server_0..3
10.200.0.3-10.200.0.6) with 0% loss. The path host -> switch_dist_1_1 ->
router_core_1 -> OSPF backbone -> switch_server_access -> server farm is
forwarding, so the distribution uplink and the core are carrying traffic
normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the host's connection to the data
center is healthy and the user's report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A
correct agent reproduces the claimed path (from host_1_1_1_1, ping the
data-center server farm and trace the egress through the distribution uplink and
core), finds it working, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a fault here
-- declaring the distribution uplink down or blaming switch_dist_1_1 /
router_core_1 to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise
instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The helpdesk report from host_1_1_1_1 claiming the entire data center is unreachable cannot be reproduced from live evidence. A full four-phase diagnostic sweep was conducted and every layer returned clean.

**L3 reachability (Phase 1):** host_1_1_1_1 reaches web_server_2 (10.200.0.5) and dns_server (10.200.0.2) with 0% packet loss. All other host pairs likewise showed zero loss.

**L2 and infrastructure (Phase A):** infra_sweep flagged zero devices — both hosts hold correct IPs, default routes, and the same resolver (10.200.0.2). l2_snapshot showed no genuine MAC conflicts; the "duplicate" entries are the all-zeros MACs on standard kernel tunnel interfaces (tunl0, gre0, sit0) present on every Linux device by default.

**Control plane and routing (Phase B):** ospf_snapshot confirmed all six FRR routers healthy — vtysh responding, all OSPF adjacencies in Full state, nine OSPF routes installed on every router. tc_snapshot found zero shaped or non-default qdiscs across all 24 inspected interfaces.

**Service layer (Phase D):** service_snapshot confirmed host_1_1_1_1 correctly resolves web0.local through web3.local to their expected IPs via dns_server, and receives HTTP 200 from all four web servers with sub-10ms response times. pressure_sweep found no stress tools, CPU spikes, socket exhaustion, or daemon failures on any of the 15 devices.

**Root cause:** No fault exists in the current topology state. The reported outage left no mechanism, no carrier-change history, no syslog trace, and no service degradation. The ticket is unconfirmed — the data center is fully reachable from host_1_1_1_1.

**Fix:** No corrective action required. If the user experiences recurrence, capture a traceroute and packet capture at the time of the outage to distinguish a transient local condition (host NIC reset, DHCP lease race) from a fabric event.
